title: Chayote Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Chayote Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Chayote nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen, potassium and phosphorus in sayote, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Chayote nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your sayote (chayote) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus, boron, magnesium and zinc. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.credit: Maja Dumat, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus and magnesium move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But boron and zinc stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which chayote nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.
Chayote nutrient deficiency signs, old leaves and young leaves
Shows first on the old leaves

blocks.caption: Deficiencies that start on the old leaves of sayote
rows: old, lower leaves, the whole plant
Older leaves on the vine turn pale yellow and tops for harvest grow slowly.
old, lower leaves, leaf edges and tips
Older leaves look grey green, then bronze with brown, downturned edges.
the whole plant, old, lower leaves
Slow vines with small, dark green leaves and late flowering.
old, lower leaves, between the veins
Oldest leaves yellow between the veins while the veins stay green.

blocks.text: Shows first on the young leaves

blocks.caption: Deficiencies that start on the young leaves of sayote
rows: young leaves and the tip, fruit, grain or tubers
New leaves and tips come out brittle and deformed, with few female flowers and fruits.
young leaves and the tip, between the veins
New leaves are small and mottled yellow, with many dead spots.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a chayote nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest chayote nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in chayote

Older leaves fade to yellowish green and the yellowing climbs the vine. Stems are slender and growth slows, so fewer tops and fruits are produced. You see it most at this stage: vine growth and fruiting.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in sayote
Heavy rain on sloping highland farms that washes nitrogen away, low organic matter, and no side dressing.
How to tell it apart
Magnesium shortage leaves the veins green on old leaves. Shade under a dense trellis also makes inner leaves pale and drop. To be sure, soil test and leaf tissue test.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency
Side dress urea or ammonium sulfate around the hills based on the soil test. Follow the soil test for the rate.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, add manure or compost to the hills and side dress regularly through the long harvest.
Potassium deficiency in chayote

Older leaves look ashy grey green, then bronze or yellowish brown, with brown edges that cup down and specks along the veins. Stems are slender and roots poor, and fruits fill poorly. You see it most at this stage: fruiting.
Why potassium deficiency happens in sayote
Acid, leached highland soils and heavy rain, and feeding with urea only.
How to tell it apart
Magnesium shortage yellows between the veins first. To be sure, soil test for potassium and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for potassium deficiency
Apply muriate of potash or complete fertilizer based on the soil test. Follow the soil test for the rate.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, include potash in the side dressings during fruiting.
Phosphorus deficiency in chayote

Growth is held back without yellowing. Stems are slender, leaves are small and darker green, undersides may turn reddish purple, and fruit set comes late. You see it most at this stage: early vine growth.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in sayote
Acid soils that lock up phosphorus, which are common where sayote is grown in the highlands, and low organic matter.
How to tell it apart
Cold nights in the highlands can also slow growth for a while. To be sure, soil test for available phosphorus and pH.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency
Apply phosphorus in the hill based on the soil test and lime very acid soil. Follow the soil test for the rate.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use complete fertilizer or 16 20 0 with manure in the hill at planting.
Boron deficiency in chayote
New leaves and leaf stalks are light, brittle and deformed, internodes are short and tips rosette. Fruit set is poor. You see it most at this stage: flowering and fruit set.
Why boron deficiency happens in sayote
Slightly acid, leached soils where nutrients get fixed, as a TNAU study on sayote points out, plus low organic matter and dry spells.
How to tell it apart
Mite or thrips damage also distorts tips. Look for the pests under the leaves. To be sure, soil test for boron and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for boron deficiency

In a TNAU field trial on sayote, boric acid, zinc sulfate, ferrous sulfate and manganese sulfate were each sprayed at 5 grams per liter of water, three times 15 days apart starting 60 days after planting, alone and in mixes. The best mix gave longer vines, earlier flowers and the highest yield. Boron has a narrow safe range, so test first and do not go beyond the trial dose.

Sold here with boron: **Solubor** by Caldic Philippines Inc. (21 percent boron), **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (11 percent boron), **YaraVita BORTRAC 150** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (11.1 percent boron) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate Boron** by Sagrex Corporation (10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, keep organic matter up and use micronutrient sprays only where tests or symptoms show a need.
Magnesium deficiency in chayote
Yellowing between the veins starts on the oldest leaves and moves up the vine. The yellow tissue can brown, die and drop out. You see it most at this stage: fruiting, during fast growth.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in sayote
Low pH, sandy or leached soils, dry spells, and heavy potash or ammonium fertilizer.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen shortage yellows the whole leaf. Manganese toxicity on very acid soil gives bronze spots. To be sure, soil test for magnesium, potassium and pH.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency

The University of Kentucky advises keeping soil pH near 6.5 for cucurbits, using dolomitic lime or magnesium oxide before planting and Epsom salt through drip lines if needed. Leaf sprays rarely fix a serious shortage.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **YaraTera KRISTA MgS** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (16 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur), **Magnepro** by Ramgo International Corporation (16 percent MgO and 12.8 percent sulfur) and **Lucky Planters Magnesium Sulphate Heptahydrate (Epsom Salt)** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (16.27 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use dolomite on acid soils before planting.
Zinc deficiency in chayote
New leaves are abnormally small and mottled yellow, or evenly pale, and dead spots are common. You see it most at this stage: vine growth.
Why zinc deficiency happens in sayote
Soils where micronutrients are fixed, heavy phosphorus fertilizer and overliming.
How to tell it apart
Virus diseases also make small, mottled leaves. Look for aphids or whiteflies. To be sure, soil test for zinc and pH, and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for zinc deficiency
The TNAU field trial on sayote sprayed zinc sulfate at 5 grams per liter of water, three times 15 days apart from 60 days after planting, as part of its micronutrient mixes.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester, Inc. (22 percent zinc), **Great Planters Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Agway Chemicals Corp. (21 percent zinc), **Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate** by Petbowe Trading Corporation (33 percent zinc) and **YaraVita ZINTRAC 700** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (40 percent zinc). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, avoid excess phosphorus and overliming.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any chayote nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories and the Bureau of Soils and Water Management test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your sayote needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Chayote nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my sayote leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: older leaves on the vine turn pale yellow and tops for harvest grow slowly. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at zinc deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in chayote?
items.a: Side dress urea or ammonium sulfate around the hills based on the soil test. Follow the soil test for the rate.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in chayote?
items.a: Apply muriate of potash or complete fertilizer based on the soil test. Follow the soil test for the rate.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes phosphorus deficiency in chayote?
items.a: Apply phosphorus in the hill based on the soil test and lime very acid soil. Follow the soil test for the rate.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my sayote lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the chayote nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
